close_reason: Fixed in commit b1be5a3: helpers_compile #[cfg(test)] block removed from helpers.rs across all 6 sibling client crates.
description:
tests/helpers.rs:63-77 contains `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { fn helpers_compile }`. Both tests/calendar_smoke_tests.rs:9 and tests/availability_tests.rs:6 do `#[path = "helpers.rs"] mod helpers;`. Result: each integration test binary picks up that test, plus the helpers.rs file itself produces a third binary, leading to `cargo test` output:

  Running tests/helpers.rs        → tests::helpers_compile … ok
  Running tests/calendar_smoke_tests.rs → calendar_smoke + helpers::tests::helpers_compile (ok)
  Running tests/availability_tests.rs → availability_round_trip + helpers::tests::helpers_compile (ok)

Three runs of the same test, three binaries linked. Adds compile time and noise.

Two cleaner options:
1. Drop the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block from helpers.rs entirely. Compile-failure of the helpers will already be caught the moment any consuming test file fails to compile.
2. Move helpers into tests/common/mod.rs and use `mod common;` in each test file (Rust idiomatic test-helper layout — does NOT compile common as its own binary).

Option 2 is more idiomatic. The current `#[path = "helpers.rs"]` workaround exists specifically because /tests/*.rs is each its own binary.
title: helpers_compile test runs three times because of #[path] include
